title: Base change of the Kummer coefficients
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], let $k$ be
algebraically closed, let $N\geq1$, and let $A$ be a finite
$\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z$-module which is free of finite rank (for
instance $A=A_{E,n}$ with $N=n\cdot v_\ell(\varpi_E)$ under the
hypothesis $e(E/\Ql)\mid n$ of [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]). For every
smooth separated curve $C$ over $k$ and every
integer $q\geq0$, the natural map

$$
H^q(C_{\Et},\mu_{\ell^N})\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A
\longrightarrow
H^q(C_{\Et},\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A)
$$

is an isomorphism. Here $A$ denotes the constant sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf] when it occurs in a sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and cohomology is that of underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. More precisely, put $m=\ell^N$, $R=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$, and $F=\mu_m$, the kernel in [def-sc-kummer-sequence]. The map $\beta_A^q$ displayed above is characterized by
$$
\beta_A^q(x\otimes a)=H^q(i_a)(x),\qquad i_a:F\longrightarrow F\otimes_R A,\quad z\longmapsto z\otimes a.
$$
Compatibility with Kummer boundaries has the following precise meaning. Write $\partial^q:H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\to H^{q+1}(C_{\Et},F)$ for the boundary of the ordinary Kummer sequence. For any finite free abelian group $L$ and any isomorphism $L/mL\cong A$, take that Kummer sequence tensored over $\mathbf Z$ with $L$, which is a finite direct sum of the ordinary sequence. Identify its left term $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L$ with $F\otimes_R A$. Its cohomology boundary, using $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L)\cong H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L$, descends to a map
$$
\partial_A^q:H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\longrightarrow H^{q+1}(C_{\Et},F\otimes_R A).
$$
This map is independent of the lift $L$ and satisfies, for every $u$ and $a$,
$$
\partial_A^q(u\otimes a)=\beta_A^{q+1}(\partial^q(u)\otimes a).
$$
Thus coefficient compatibility includes the usual units Kummer class in degree one. It does not require an $R$-module structure on $\mathbf G_m$.

proof.text: The finite-field characteristic and l != p imply that l^N is a unit on C, by mapping the corresponding field unit along the structure morphism on global sections. Apply the normalized finite-free cohomology comparison to obtain beta in every degree.

Define delta on pure tensors by beta(partial(x) tensor a). The tensor universal property over Z applies because the Kummer boundary and beta are additive. This constructs delta directly and proves its required pure-tensor formula.

For each specified integral lift L with basis b and reduction e, take the short exact finite biproduct Kummer sequence and its normalized integral cohomology comparison alpha. The reduced integral dual basis gives the normalized left-term sheaf isomorphism theta.

For l in L, form the morphism of short complexes whose three components are sum_j b_j^*(l) inclusion_j. The biproduct identities prove commutativity with both Kummer arrows. The normalized theta formula and the basis expansion identify its left component followed by theta with i_(e([l])). Sheaf.H.map_deltaSucc naturality identifies the lifted boundary with H(i_(e([l])))(partial(x)), which equals delta(x tensor e([l])) by the beta and delta formulas. This proves the entire integral-lift clause. Pure tensors generate, so the formula also makes the result independent of the chosen lift and basis.

proof_origin.place: Finite-direct-sum argument, implemented by explicit dual bases and naturality of Sheaf.H.deltaSucc. Finite-biproduct exactness replaces the generic flatness route; integral coordinates modulo m replace the generic quotient-ring tensor route. R1 stage 3, 2026-10-19.

tool_uses.why: General additivity and naturality of the cohomology delta-functor; a homological algebra tool for the finite-sum argument, not a replacement of any unit step. No node of this unit states this general theorem.
Only its tensor-unit isomorphism is used to establish flatness of the constant integral unit; this generic ringed-site tool does not replace any unit argument.
Closure of flat sheaves under coproducts proves that the chosen finite free integral lift tensors exact sequences exactly; no node of the Kummer unit states that general ringed-site fact.
Its bilinear universal property realizes the quotient-ring tensor maps as actual sheaf maps; a generic site tensor tool, not a replacement route.

statement_correction.what: The imported proof tensors the ordinary Kummer sequence with A over R = Z/ell^N, but G_m is not an R-module; tensoring its middle terms over Z with A instead makes both zero. Replace that ill-typed boundary clause by the boundary of the sequence tensored with a finite free integral lift L, descended along L -> L/ell^N L = A. The original cohomology comparison and all its hypotheses are retained.

Coefficient category: abelian sheaves on C_Et with the R-action on mu_m, the sheafified tensor with constant A, and K-injective cohomology, which step 1 reduces to R^q Gamma through the leaf. I checked the inverse formulas both ways in steps 3 and 6. Step 5: flatness follows from the unit isomorphism and the coproduct-flat node. Step 7: theta and its inverse come from quotient-ring clause (2) and the bilinear universal property; the inverse does not depend on the lift because mz=0 and its target is killed by m. Step 8: I recomputed the naturality square for the insertion morphism; it gives the boundary formula exactly. Step 9: the descent is elementary. Edge cases tested: A=0, q=0, empty C, disconnected C, and C=G_m. The statement is unchanged; its integral-lift correction is valid because G_m tensor Z/m is 0 as an etale sheaf. There are no new nodes and I found no duplicates. lean.statement: theorem kummer_coefficient_base_change (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) [IsCurve f] [Smooth f] (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N)))) [Module.Free (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))) A] [Module.Finite (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))) A] : ∃ (hm : IsUnit ((P.coefficients.l ^ N : ℕ) : Γ(C, ⊤))) (beta : ∀ q : ℕ, (Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (P.coefficients.l ^ N)) q ⊗[ ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))] A) ≃ₗ[ ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))] Sheaf.H ((kummerAbelianTwist C (P.coefficients.l ^ N)).obj A) q), (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (P.coefficients.l ^ N)) q) (a : A), beta q (x ⊗ₜ a) = Sheaf.H.map (kummerCoefficientInsertion C (P.coefficients.l ^ N) A a) q x) ∧ ∃ delta : ∀ q : ℕ, (Sheaf.H C.gmSheaf q ⊗[ℤ] A) →+ Sheaf.H ((kummerAbelianTwist C (P.coefficients.l ^ N)).obj A) (q + 1), (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : Sheaf.H C.gmSheaf q) (a : A), delta q (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] a) = beta (q + 1) (Sheaf.H.δSucc (C.kummerSequence_shortExact (P.coefficients.l ^ N) hm) q x ⊗ₜ a)) ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, KummerIntegralLiftBoundary C (P.coefficients.l ^ N) q A (delta q)
lean.note: The published KummerModuleCoefficients interface is reused and its landed node is added to stmt_deps. The integral-lift boundary clause is encoded in any finite integral basis by the finite biproduct of the ordinary Kummer sequence. Both identifications are normalized on generators. The only new helper definition is the explicit Prop KummerIntegralLiftBoundary; no tensor or cohomology object is redefined. The illustrative coefficient example lem-pur-finite-kummer-level is not needed to state the result for arbitrary finite free A.
